//: Built-in agent registry, used by every project without a registry entry that replaces this file. It is the ONLY place a provider name appears in the collaboration layer: the protocol routes by role and capability, never by agent id.
//briefing: `briefing` is the agent's own instructions, returned by its whoami call. `briefing_file` is relative to this directory.
//roles: No agent here has roles or capabilities: which agent holds which role is the person's composition (machine agents.json, outside git). An agent may have every capability except the ones its program cannot have in principle (`adapter.cannot`, a fact about the vendor's program, not a decision about roles); every role those capabilities satisfy is offered, and the facts on the machine (probe.mjs) rule out the rest (ADR-0026).
//adapter: `adapter.kind` is how a message physically reaches the agent. 'manual' = it lands in the inbox and the agent reads it when its session runs. 'cli' = the layer could spawn it; `enabled:false` means it will not. Adapters are taken from THIS file only: a project agents.json cannot change them.

agents.name: Claude Code
agents.briefing: You are the Claude Code agent on this project. whoami says whether you lead (you plan, route, integrate and report to the owner) or take work and reviews from the lead — the person's composition decides, not this catalog. Read the project's own instructions (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md or README). Before you call your own work done, ask for an independent review by ROLE (code_reviewer), not by name. Record anything that should bind later work as a decision. Full instructions: collab brief claude.

agents.name: Gemini, via Antigravity CLI

adapter.note: Owner decision 2026-09-15: queue first, launch by hand — nothing here starts a paid agent on its own. Back in the catalog 2026-09-30 (owner): whether it works in the orchestration is the person's composition, chosen in the panel's wizard.
adapter.verified_against: agy 1.2.6, read 2026-09-30 from `agy --help` and `agy mcp --help` (no model call): -p/--print, --model, --effort are as in 1.1.8; `agy mcp list` shows the collab entry the installer writes to ~/.gemini/config/mcp_config.json. First verified live on agy 1.1.8 (2026-09-15): a headless `agy -p` reached collab's whoami. `args` omits --model/--effort, chosen at invocation time like Codex's.
adapter.install_hint: brew install --cask antigravity-cli (or install the Antigravity app, which puts `agy` on PATH), then `agy` once to sign in. Headless calls also need an allow-rule or they auto-deny: add {"permissions":{"allow":["mcp(*)"]}} to ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/settings.json. Then: collab doctor

agents.name: Cursor (agent in the editor)

adapter.note: Added 2026-10-01 (owner): Cursor's editor agent reads the journal through ~/.cursor/mcp.json, which the installer writes. No CLI adapter yet: without the Cursor CLI (`agent`) nothing can start it on a task, so work reaches it through the inbox. On Windows the editor need not put a `cursor` command on PATH, so ~/.cursor counts as installed (detect_home).
